A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, comparison table, experimental plots, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison after matching pagination and relocated content.

before.justification: V3 reports original GD experiments on noisy 2-XOR data, varying sample size and dimension and presenting test errors in Figure 1.

after.justification: V4 retains the original noisy 2-XOR experiments and their test-error plots in Section 5 and Figure 1.

M1.justification: The ReLU architecture, symmetric initialization, fixed output weights, logistic objective, and GD updates remain unchanged. The revised width requirements concern theoretical guarantees rather than an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same noisy 2-XOR classification distribution, varying n at d = 6 and varying d at n = 64. No dataset, domain, or task scenario is added.

E2.justification: Section 5 introduces no empirical comparator in either version. Table 1 retains the same prior-work rows; its revisions concern cited analytical bounds rather than comparator membership.

E3.justification: Both report two-layer networks with width 128, 500 GD iterations, and step size 0.1, evaluating population loss over all 2^d distribution points. The reported experimental procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The same sample-size and dimension sweeps support the d²/n scaling analysis. No ablation, robustness test, error analysis, or case study is added or removed, including in the appendices.

E5.justification: The scatterplots and linear-fit reporting are unchanged. Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The experimental plot images are identical. Both retain fitted lines 0.1428x − 0.0199 and 0.1648x − 0.0241, and the same interpretation of test error as approximately 0.15d²/n.

T1.justification: Theorems 2 and 3 add a multiplicative n³ width requirement. Appendix C replaces Lemma 22's matrix-factorization proof with initialization linearization and remainder control, changing its bound from order L²√(F(Wbar) log(m)/n) to √(F(Wbar)/n). The final population-risk rates remain unchanged under stronger hypotheses. Appendix B also restores a missing aᵀ factor in Lemma 19's expansion.

C1.justification: V3 explicitly claims optimal generalization with width polylogarithmic in n; v4 removes that contribution and retains the risk rate under stronger width requirements. It also removes the claim of having the best generalization bound and width condition, while strengthening the intermediate Rademacher claim to omit explicit depth dependence.

C2.justification: Remark 2 replaces the sparse-matrix explanation of the Rademacher bound with approximate linearity near initialization. It newly explains why the shallow-network activated/nonactivated-neuron argument does not directly extend and leaves polylogarithmic width as an open problem, substantially changing the stated boundary of the central guarantee.

D1.justification: The experimental parameters, Google Colab execution note, and reproduction-notebook/repository access information are retained. No implementation, hardware, timing, or resource-access details are added.

R1.justification: The introduction, Table 1, and Remarks 2 and 6 now credit Chen et al. with a polynomial-depth alternative bound, whereas v3 presented only an exponential-depth, width-dependent bound. This materially revises the central comparison and claimed advantages. V4 also discusses the distinction from Lei et al.'s shallow-network analysis; the cited-work set remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The contribution summary and Remarks 2 and 6 are locally rewritten, and Appendix C's proof exposition is replaced and shortened. The title, abstract, main section sequence, and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands the Chen et al. entry into a taller, multiline display. The unchanged experimental panels move from page 10 to page 9, with accompanying text, equation, and reference reflow. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: Appendix C removes v3's unsupported treatment of input-dependent matrices as common factors in a Rademacher sum, replacing it with linearization and remainder control. Theorems 2 and 3 disclose the n³ width cost, and Remark 2 withdraws the polylogarithmic-width guarantee. This substantially repairs the central argument and calibrates its scope. Table 1 still omits n³ from the 'Ours' width entry, leaving an important summary inconsistency.
